rows.en: Yamato: "Well, we should be nearing the Holy Land, right?
Shouldn't we go to the bridge, meow?"
Touya: "Yeah, you're right."
Bernst: "Oh, if I remember correctly... it was Touya, wasn't it?"
Touya: "? Come to think of it, did I introduce myself?"
Bernst: "No. I asked Ymir."
Touya: "I see."
Bernst: "Do you have a moment?"
Touya: "Sure. Want to come into my room, then?"
Bernst: "No, I only want to ask a few questions,
so here will be fine."
Touya: "...Questions? Is that part of your research, too?"
Bernst: "Yes, though there's a personal element to it as well.
Then, without further ado...
What are you fighting for?"
Touya: "That's sudden... What do you mean?"
Bernst: "My apologies. That's just my nature...
You're not from this world, are you?
In other words, until very recently, war and fighting
had nothing to do with your life, correct?
Yet now you pilot a Spirit Mech and fight... Why?"
Touya: "...It's not like I'm fighting because I want to.
I came here, didn't know what the hell was going on, and before I knew it,
I was fighting. That's the truth of it, but it's reality now.
I could reject it and run away,
but that wouldn't solve a damn thing.
If there's something I can do now, I'll give it everything I've got
and try... Well, I guess that's why I fight."
Bernst: "I see... So you don't question
the act of fighting?"
Touya: "That's not true. I'm scared of going on fighting
until people dying starts to seem normal."
Bernst: "But you are fighting now.
Do you think meeting force with force
will solve things?
Don't you think it will only increase hatred and ultimately
lead to more fighting?"
Touya: "I don't really understand complicated stuff.
I guess people just aren't that well made.
Even in my world, there was always a conflict going on somewhere.
As long as people have a competitive streak and so on, those conflicts won't disappear."
Bernst: "Exactly! That's the point.
As long as people retain 'individuality,'
there will inevitably be an 'other.'
In other words, there are the worlds of 'self' and 'other,'
two separate worlds.
Those worlds can never be reconciled.
To protect the 'self,' rejecting the 'other'
is the only choice. That is where conflict arises.
That's why human history is also a history of fighting."
Touya: "But couldn't you accept that 'other'
instead?
You can acknowledge another person, can't you?"
Bernst: "Yes. But that's only on the surface.
On a fundamental level, within the 'self,'
it means defeat.
Very few people can bear that humiliation."
Touya: "...Well, I'm not going to tell you what to think,
but what are you getting at?"
Bernst: "...My apologies. In short,
isn't it inevitable that people fight?
Whatever reasons they give, people keep fighting.
That's how they grow, little by little.
It's not something for someone to intervene in and accelerate.
Even if it keeps producing hatred,
the greatness of humanity lies in overcoming it.
Don't you agree?"
Touya: "...Is there some arrogant bastard
like that close to you?"
Bernst: "...Yes. An old acquaintance.
Well, we're still acquainted now, of course."
Touya: "You make it sound like there's more to it."
Bernst: "Heh heh... 'Humanity, immersed in freedom and peace, loses its sense of tension
and merely tumbles down the slope toward decadence.
Battle promotes growth both physical and mental.
It is battle that gives people vigor and discipline, and helps
accelerate the development of civilization...' So some people say.
I find something to sympathize with in that view, too."
Touya: "I'm glad you're not some blind worshipper of war.
Sure, what you're saying might be one of the truths
that history so far bears out.
But just because that's how it's been until now,
doesn't mean it has to stay that way, does it?"
Bernst: "That is what I'm hoping for, too.
That humanity will find a better path through something other than fighting.
Touya. I'm glad we could talk.
It seems my heart lies somewhere close to yours.
You may find yourself remembering this conversation before long.
When that happens, I would like your help.
I don't think it will be a bad deal for you and your friends."
Touya: "There's too much you're leaving unclear.
You can't expect me to agree to help you on that basis."
Bernst: "I'm not asking for an answer now.
It will be enough if you ultimately help me.
...I've spent a very worthwhile time here today.
Thank you. Until next time."
Touya: "H-Hey! Don't just decide we're finished!"
Yamato: "...He's gone."
Touya: "...Who the hell is that guy...?"

review_batches.context: Examined0-83 and complete99-row Bernst/Touya discussion plus prior philosophical encounter context. Asked why fights, reluctant current reality, fear of normalized deaths, self/other and conflict arguments, forced-growth objection, outside battle-growth view and partial sympathy.
review_batches.decisions: All philosophical human-nature/history claims attributed speakers and challenged, not objective science or narrator prescription. Preserve two rhetorical worlds, conditional/concessive argument and not-forced-intervention versus partial sympathy tension. Full pro-drop subjects/directions, genuine transitions flagged. No named identity for old acquaintance or guaranteed world-law.
